name: Flickr Pro
tagline: Host a personal photo gallery and metadata archive on user-owned storage

pricing.notes: Annual Pro plan divided by 12; exact list price can change.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Flickr Pro, host a personal photo gallery and metadata archive on user-owned storage. The hard boundary is large photography community, discovery, hosting, moderation, and mobile apps, plus image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish.
coreLoopDIY: Catalog local photos into a personal gallery and metadata archive on user-owned storage, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
whatYouLose: large photography community, discovery, hosting, moderation, and mobile apps
moatNotes: image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish
ongoingBurden: raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Flickr Pro because photographers pay because image quality, catalog safety, and fast handling of huge libraries matter more than cloning sliders. The recurring cost buys raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Immich
priorArt.desc: Active open-source self-hosted photo and video management platform.

alternatives.name: Immich
alternatives.desc: A superb personal photo archive with mobile backup, metadata, albums, search, maps, and sharing on storage you control; public portfolio polish is modest.

alternatives.name: LibrePhotos
alternatives.desc: Self-hosted photos and video with faces, objects, semantic search, albums, and public links; deployment is a small server, not a button.

alternatives.name: Lychee
alternatives.desc: A clean self-hosted album gallery with metadata, passworded sharing, downloads, and a simple Docker setup; much less discovery machinery.

alternatives.name: PhotoPrism
alternatives.desc: A searchable self-hosted photo library with RAW support, labels, faces, maps, albums, metadata, and share links; library first, social network never.

alternatives.name: Photoview
alternatives.desc: Maps existing folders directly into a clean web gallery with RAW, EXIF, users, albums, links, and downloads; your directory tree stays the boss.

alternatives.name: Piwigo
alternatives.desc: The old, dependable gallery engine: private albums, users, metadata, themes, plugins, and mobile upload, paid for in maintenance rather than money.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Flickr Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free account caps the library at 1,000 items, allows only 50 non-public items, and forbids commercial use; that is not a Pro archive.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal local photo catalog DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Flickr Pro in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, Rust image libraries, SQLite, and local filesystem access; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: catalog local photos into a personal gallery and metadata archive on user-owned storage, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments, and export selected originals or rendered copies.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Index selected folders without moving or rewriting originals and store only catalog data in SQLite.
Generate thumbnails and previews, read EXIF, detect duplicates by hash, and monitor file changes.
Provide timeline, folders, albums, ratings, flags, tags, search, and side-by-side compare.
Store edits as reversible parameters for crop, rotate, exposure, contrast, white balance, and saturation.
Render exports to a new folder with explicit color space, quality, size, and metadata choices.
Add catalog backup, missing-file repair, integrity scan, and a clear original-safety guarantee.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a proprietary raw-rendering engine.
Deliberately leave out hosted cross-device photo sync and client galleries.
Deliberately leave out frontier culling, retouching, and generative models.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
